trick: Management is a profession in some respects and not in others — it has a body of knowledge and training, but no compulsory qualification and no enforceable code, so the standard answer is 'not a full-fledged profession'. Effectiveness is finishing the task; efficiency is finishing it cheaply. A manager needs both, and questions test the difference in one line.

video.query: nature and significance of management effectiveness efficiency class 12 business studies

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the nature of management.

items.statement: Effectiveness means completing the task on time, whatever the cost.
items.why: Effectiveness is about achieving the end result. Efficiency is about doing it with least cost — the two can pull apart.

items.statement: Management is a full-fledged profession like medicine or law.
items.why: There is a body of knowledge and there are associations, but no restricted entry and no legally enforceable code of conduct.

items.statement: Management is both a science and an art.
items.why: It has systematised principles like a science and demands personal skill and judgement like an art.

items.statement: Management is intangible — you see its results, not the thing itself.
items.why: Its presence is felt through order in the workplace and targets met.

items.statement: Top-level management is chiefly concerned with supervising workers directly.
items.why: That is supervisory or lower-level management. Top level sets objectives and strategy.

trick: Keep Fayol and Taylor apart: Fayol gave 14 general PRINCIPLES from the top of the organisation down, Taylor gave scientific management TECHNIQUES from the shop floor up. Unity of command means one boss per employee; unity of direction means one head and one plan per group of activities — those two get swapped more than any other pair.

trick: Planning is the first function and it is future-oriented, but it does not guarantee success and it does not remove risk — it only prepares for it. Distinguish the plan types: a policy is a general guide, a procedure is the sequence of steps, a rule is a hard do-or-don't, and a budget is a plan stated in numbers.

A comprehensive plan for meeting the competition and reaching the objective

The chronological sequence of steps for carrying out a task
A specific statement of what must or must not be done, allowing no discretion
The prescribed way of performing one step of a procedure
A plan expressed in numbers, which is also a means of control
A detailed statement of the objectives, policies, procedures and resources for a course of action

trick: Delegation has three elements and they must be equal: authority, responsibility and accountability. Authority can be delegated, responsibility cannot be escaped, and accountability always flows upward — a manager who delegates a task remains answerable for it. That single sentence answers most questions here.

video.query: organising structure delegation authority responsibility accountability class 12

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about organising and delegation.

items.statement: A manager who delegates a task is no longer answerable for it.
items.why: Accountability cannot be delegated. The superior remains answerable to his own superior for the result.

items.statement: Authority flows downward while accountability flows upward.
items.why: The superior grants authority down the chain and the subordinate answers back up it.

items.statement: Decentralisation is the same thing as delegation.
items.why: Delegation is between two individuals; decentralisation is an organisation-wide policy of pushing authority down to lower levels.

items.statement: Functional structure groups jobs of a similar nature together.
items.why: All production in one department, all marketing in another — efficient, but it can breed departmental rather than organisational loyalty.

items.statement: Divisional structure suits an organisation with several product lines.
items.why: Each division handles one product with its own functions, so performance can be measured product by product.

trick: Recruitment attracts and selection rejects — recruitment is positive, selection is negative. Training improves skills for the present job, development prepares the whole person for future responsibility. On-the-job methods teach by doing (apprenticeship, internship); off-the-job methods teach away from the workplace (lectures, case studies).

trick: Maslow's needs are satisfied in order and a satisfied need stops motivating — that is the whole theory in one line. The order is physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation. Financial incentives buy the lower needs; non-financial ones like status, recognition and job enrichment reach the higher ones.

video.query: maslow hierarchy of needs financial and non financial incentives class 12

data.prompt: Put Maslow's hierarchy in order from the lowest need upward.

items.label: Physiological needs
items.note: Hunger, thirst, shelter — met by the basic wage

items.label: Social or affiliation needs
items.note: Belonging, friendship, acceptance by the group

items.label: Self-actualisation needs
items.note: Becoming what one is capable of becoming — growth and self-fulfilment

trick: Planning and controlling are inseparable: planning is looking ahead, controlling is looking back, and controlling without a plan has no standard to measure against. Management by exception means only significant deviations reach the manager — do not confuse it with management by objectives.

video.query: controlling process steps management by exception class 12 business studies

data.prompt: Put the steps of the controlling process in order.

items.label: Setting performance standards
items.note: Quantitative where possible — units, cost, time

items.label: Measurement of actual performance
items.note: Objectively and in the same units as the standard

items.label: Analysing deviations
items.note: Critical point control and management by exception decide which deviations matter

items.label: Taking corrective action
items.note: Fix the deviation, or revise the standard if it was unrealistic

trick: Capital market is long-term, money market is short-term — that one line sorts the instruments. Treasury bills, commercial paper and call money are money market; shares and debentures are capital market. The primary market is where securities are issued for the first time; the secondary market is where existing ones change hands.
